exchanges.body:
Hotfix for the duplicates. Can someone approve fast? No time for tests.

```diff
+++ billing/emit.py
 def finalize_invoice(invoice, endpoints, outbox):
+    if any(e["invoice_id"] == invoice["id"] for e in outbox.events):
+        return
     for url in endpoints:
         outbox.add(invoice["id"], "webhook", url)
+++ migrations/0042_dedupe.py
+def upgrade():
+    op.create_index("outbound_events_dedupe", "outbound_events", ["invoice_id", "kind", "target"], unique=True)
```

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks for jumping on it, but I don't think we should merge this. (1) The any() check then add is check-then-act: two workers handling the same redelivered task both see nothing and both send, which is exactly what happened at 10:04 (14 of the 41 were parallel). (2) The migration builds the unique index without CONCURRENTLY, which locks outbound_events (~40 writes/s) for the whole build, and it will fail anyway because the 41 duplicate rows already exist. #1496 (opened yesterday) does this properly: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a unique key, deletes existing duplicates, then CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in an autocommit block, with a parallel test. Marcus, can we take #1496 as the emergency change?

versions.content:
"""PG17 safe search_path (Platform's PG17 checklist, item 1).

The reminders_local_day expression index (0031) calls reminder_local_day(), which calls canonical_tz() unqualified,
which reads tz_aliases unqualified. PG17 runs ANALYZE, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE INDEX with search_path =
pg_catalog, pg_temp, so both lookups fail there. Pin each function's search path; no table is touched.
"""
from alembic import op

revision = "0043"
down_revision = "0042"


def upgrade():
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.canonical_tz(text) SET search_path = public, pg_temp")
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text) SET search_path = public, pg_temp")


def downgrade():
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.reminder_local_day(timestamptz, text) RESET search_path")
    op.execute("ALTER FUNCTION public.canonical_tz(text) RESET search_path")
